the_cage.description: 5 specific policy changes that, once enacted, retroactively catch every flagged MP, lobbyist, and official documented on this site

policies.name: Public Officer Accountability Act
policies.what: Strengthen Criminal Code s.122 (Breach of Trust by Public Officer) with mandatory minimum sentences for procurement corruption exceeding $10M or obstruction of oversight bodies. Require RCMP to investigate within 90 days of Ethics Commissioner findings.
policies.who_it_catches: SDTC board (186 conflicts), ArriveCAN contractors, Provost Marshal Trudeau (obstruction), officials who approved arms exports contradicting public statements
policies.who_pushes_it: CPC MPs — they already want to punish Liberal procurement scandals. Give them the tool and they'll build the cage themselves
policies.trap: The same mechanism catches CPC officials documented in lobbying data when they inevitably take power

policies.name: Foreign Lobbying Transparency Act
policies.what: Require all organizations conducting 100+ annual lobbying communications to disclose: funding sources, foreign government connections, trip sponsorships to officials, and subject matter per meeting
policies.who_it_catches: CIJA (2,156 comms, 993 officials, 73 MP trips), Brookfield network (120 comms while board chair advised PM), defense contractors (2,763 combined comms)
policies.who_pushes_it: LPC MPs — frame it as strengthening Bill C-70 (Foreign Interference Act) which they already passed. They think it targets China. It actually targets everyone including CIJA and Brookfield
policies.trap: The transparency requirements expose the exact lobbying concentration patterns we've already documented but which currently require CSV mining to find

policies.name: Revolving Door Prohibition
policies.what: 10-year cooling period before former Ministers, Deputy Ministers, or ADMs can register as lobbyists for any entity they regulated. Criminal penalty for violation
policies.who_it_catches: David Pratt (ex-Defence Minister → Raytheon/IAI lobbyist, 408 DND comms), Dominic Barton (McKinsey → Ambassador → advisory chair), future Carney post-PM lobbying
policies.who_pushes_it: NDP and Bloc — they have the least revolving door exposure and can position this as anti-corruption. Clean CPC/LPC backbenchers support it because it doesn't affect them
policies.trap: Retroactive application catches the current revolving door operators and prevents future ones regardless of party

policies.name: PM Corporate Divestiture Act
policies.what: Require sitting PMs to fully divest (not blind trust) all holdings exceeding $1M in any entity that lobbies the federal government. Ethics screen must cover 100% of portfolio, not 5%
policies.who_it_catches: Mark Carney specifically — $50B Brookfield conflict, 95% unscreened portfolio, NorthRiver Midstream direct lobbying
policies.who_pushes_it: CPC — they already call Carney 'Conflict Carney'. This gives them a concrete policy demand that sounds reasonable to voters
policies.trap: Applies to ALL future PMs. When CPC takes power, their leader faces the same divestiture requirement. Poilievre's refusal to get security clearance suggests he has something to hide too

policies.name: Military Oversight Independence Act
policies.what: Remove CFNIS from military chain of command. MPCC given binding investigative power with full disclosure requirements. Federal Court enforcement of oversight compliance
policies.who_it_catches: BGen Trudeau (obstruction), LCol LeBlanc (Vance clearance), future military police leadership who obstruct civilian oversight
policies.who_pushes_it: Veterans' caucus members from all parties + clean defence committee MPs. Frame as 'supporting the troops' — hard to vote against
policies.trap: Permanent structural change. Once CFNIS is independent, the self-protecting chain of command can never re-form regardless of which party governs

key_changes: LIBERAL MINORITY: Carney needs 3 more votes for confidence. Bloc (22) or NDP (7) must support.
BLOC IS KINGMAKER: With 22 seats, Blanchet can extract policy concessions as price of confidence. Anti-corruption reform is perfect Quebec nationalist positioning.
NDP DESPERATE: 7 seats, lost party status. Avi Lewis (elected March 2026) needs to differentiate or party dies. Anti-corruption is survival strategy.
POILIEVRE WEAKENED: Lost own seat, won by-election to return. 87.4% leadership review but 12.6% voted against. CPC backbenchers who survived feel emboldened.
CPC LARGEST OPPOSITION: 144 seats — largest Official Opposition in Canadian history. Massive caucus that Poilievre struggles to control.
campaign_implications: PMBs from CPC backbenchers have MORE chance of passing because Liberal minority needs opposition votes on non-confidence matters
Bloc support for reform bills could be traded for Quebec concessions — Blanchet becomes reform ally
NDP with 7 seats will co-sponsor ANYTHING that gets them media attention
Green Party (1 seat, Elizabeth May) can add moral authority — she has security clearance, Poilievre doesn't
Liberal minority means committee votes are contestable — opposition majority on every committee

campaign_sequence.description: 6-phase rollout designed to build momentum where each phase creates pressure for the next

phases.name: SEED — Media amplification
actions: Send full evidence brief to Derek Fildebrandt (Western Standard) — he amplifies to conservative media audience
Send full evidence brief to readthemaple.com — they already cover CIJA/lobbying, will amplify progressive angle
Send arms pipeline + charity data to CJPME — they'll push it through their networks
Send CFNIS command chain to military media (Esprit de Corps, Canadian Military Family Magazine)
phases.goal: Create public awareness of the data before any MP receives an email. When MPs get the email, they've already seen the data in media coverage. Makes it harder to ignore.

phases.name: RECRUIT — Clean MP allies
actions: Send evidence briefs to all 113 clean MPs (score 0) across all parties
Key targets: Roman Baber (CPC, York Centre — independent-minded), Ellis Ross (CPC, BC — Indigenous anti-establishment), new LPC backbenchers who haven't been captured yet
Frame as: 'You have a clean record. Your peers don't. Here's the evidence. Here's the reform legislation.'
Include specific Magnitsky Act brief + legal framework page link
phases.goal: Build a cross-party reform caucus of MPs with clean records who have incentive to differentiate themselves from flagged peers

phases.name: ARM — Party-specific weaponization
actions: Send CPC Tier 1 MPs the Liberal dirt package (Carney $50B, SDTC 186 conflicts, ArriveCAN, arms fraud)
Send LPC Tier 1 MPs the CPC dirt package (Poilievre 12 connections, clearance refusal, Lantsman CIJA, bot networks)
Send NDP/Bloc clean MPs the full picture (both parties' dirt)
Each email ends with the same 5 policy recommendations (P1-P5)
phases.goal: Each party attacks the other using the data. Both parties end up publicly demanding accountability reforms. The reforms they demand are the cage.

phases.name: PRESSURE — Public petition + committee referral
actions: Launch e-petition on ourcommons.ca for each of the 5 policies (P1-P5)
Clean MP allies table the petitions in Parliament
Request Ethics Committee (ETHI) study on lobbying concentration (P2)
Request Defence Committee (NDDN) study on CFNIS oversight (P5)
Media coverage of petition + committee requests amplifies pressure
phases.goal: Transform online evidence into formal parliamentary record. Once it's in committee, it can't be quietly buried.

phases.name: TRAP — Private Members' Bills
actions: Clean CPC backbencher tables PMB for P1 (Public Officer Accountability Act) — positioned as 'punishing Liberal corruption'
Clean LPC backbencher tables PMB for P2 (Foreign lobbying transparency) — positioned as 'strengthening C-70'
NDP MP tables PMB for P3 (Revolving door) — positioned as 'anti-corruption'
Clean CPC MP tables PMB for P4 (PM divestiture) — positioned as 'Conflict Carney' accountability
Veterans' caucus member tables PMB for P5 (Military oversight) — positioned as 'supporting the troops'
phases.goal: 5 PMBs from 5 different parties/caucuses, each thinking they're attacking their opponents. Each bill builds one wall of the cage.

phases.name: CLOSE — The cage locks
actions: As PMBs progress through readings, the cumulative effect becomes clear — comprehensive accountability reform
MPs who pushed individual bills can't oppose the package without looking hypocritical
The Magnitsky extension (P1) retroactively applies to documented procurement corruption
The transparency act (P2) forces disclosure of exactly what our CSV mining already found
The revolving door ban (P3) catches current operators and prevents future ones
The divestiture act (P4) forces Carney's hand on Brookfield
The military independence act (P5) permanently breaks the CFNIS self-protection loop
phases.goal: 5 walls. 1 cage. Every flagged MP helped build their own wall thinking they were building it around their opponents.

rules_of_engagement: Every email contains ONLY verified government data — zero fabrication
No email reveals the existence of the campaign strategy
No email links to email-campaign.html or report-generator.html
Each MP thinks they're receiving an independent constituent/veteran briefing
The 5 policies appear as 'recommendations' not as a coordinated legislative package
Media contacts receive evidence only — never strategy
Clean MP allies are recruited individually — they never see the full campaign map
The campaign succeeds even if only 2-3 of the 5 policies pass — each wall of the cage has independent value

legal_reality.magnitsky_limitation: CRITICAL: The Magnitsky Act (JVCFOA) ONLY applies to FOREIGN nationals. It CANNOT freeze Canadian officials assets. 70 individuals listed — ALL foreign. The cage must use different tools.

criminal_code_s122.name: Breach of Trust by Public Officer (s.122)
criminal_code_s122.standard: Serious and marked departure from expected standards + dishonest/corrupt purpose
criminal_code_s122.applies_to: SDTC board (186 conflicts), Provost Marshal Trudeau (obstruction), officials who approved contradictory arms exports
criminal_code_s122.precedent: Prosecutors and public officials have been convicted under this section

criminal_code_s504.name: Private Prosecution — Lay Information Under Oath (s.504)
criminal_code_s504.what: ANY citizen can lay an information before a justice if they have reasonable grounds to believe an indictable offence was committed
criminal_code_s504.power: Constitutional safeguard against inertia or partiality on the part of authority
criminal_code_s504.limitation: AG can intervene and stay the prosecution
criminal_code_s504.strategic_value: Even if stayed, it forces public attention and creates official record. Best used as POLITICAL tool.

criminal_code_s121.name: Frauds on the Government (s.121)
criminal_code_s121.what: Bribery, fraud, corruption involving government contracts
criminal_code_s121.applies_to: ArriveCAN contractors, SDTC board members, McKinsey non-competitive contracts

conflict_of_interest_act.name: Conflict of Interest Act (reform needed)
conflict_of_interest_act.needed_reform: 10-year cooling period, full divestiture for PM, criminal penalty for violation
conflict_of_interest_act.applies_to: Carney Brookfield conflict, David Pratt revolving door

lobbying_act_reformed.name: Lobbying Act (reformed January 2026)
lobbying_act_reformed.new_threshold: 8 hours in any 4-week period triggers registration requirement
lobbying_act_reformed.cooling_period: 5-year lobbying ban for former Designated Public Office Holders
lobbying_act_reformed.enforcement_needed: The law exists — enforcement is the cage
lobbying_act_reformed.applies_to: CIJA (2,156 comms), Brookfield network, all sector lobbying

bill_c70.name: Foreign Influence Transparency and Accountability Act (C-70)
bill_c70.status: Royal Assent June 2024, registry regulations published Jan 2026
bill_c70.what: Foreign agent registry — requires registration of foreign influence activities
bill_c70.applies_to: CIJA (if acting on behalf of Israel government), Brookfield international operations, any org conducting foreign influence
bill_c70.enforcement_deadline: Registry operational target was June 2025, delayed by election
